Method of Attack: Installed on Short Message Service Center (SMSC) Linux servers to steal SMS message content and call records
Monitors incoming and outgoing connections, parses SCTP, SCCP, and TCAP traffic layers to extract SMS messages
Searches for text files with identifiers (IMSI numbers, phone numbers, keywords) to filter messages of interest
Encrypts matched messages using XOR cipher and stores them in CSV format for later theft
Accesses databases containing call records to query, save, and steal records
Impacted Systems: Linux Short Message Service Center (SMSC) servers
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of files named 'keyword_parm' and 'parm' containing message identifiers
Encrypted SMS message data stored in CSV files under /etc directory
Monitoring of SCTP, SCCP, and TCAP traffic layers
